name: UNITED AIRLINES INC
entity_filed: UAL Corporation and 27 U.S. subsidiaries, including United Air Lines, Inc.
docket: Case Nos. 02-48191 through 02-48218 (In re UAL Corporation, et al.)
same_company_evidence: Payee EIN 74-2099724 matches SEC registrant UNITED AIRLINES, INC. (CIK 0000319687), whose former names are CONTINENTAL AIRLINES, INC. and CONTINENTAL AIRLINES INC /DE/; that entity is the post-merger operating airline, HQ Chicago. Payee city of Dallas, TX is an accounts-payable address, not an operating site.
ohio_outcome: No Ohio effect at issue; the airline emerged from Chapter 11 on 2006-02-01 and was operating when the 2024 grant was paid.
source: UAL Corporation Form 8-K filed 2002-12-09 (Item 3, Bankruptcy or Receivership), SEC Archives 0000100517-02-000079; SEC EDGAR submissions API CIK 0000319687 and 0000100517; Google News RSS
notes: Three flagged headlines, none a current failure. The TheStreet piece is retrospective ('filed for bankruptcy 22 years ago'), pointing to the December 2002 UAL Corporation Chapter 11, which is 22 years before the single 2024 grant year. The two 2025 headlines are about SPIRIT Airlines' bankruptcy, with United named only as a competitor adding Orlando flights and declining to bid on Spirit's assets. Note the payee EIN was Continental Airlines' EIN; Continental's own Chapter 11 cases (1983 and 1990) are also decades before the grant.

name: WASHINGTON COUNTY CAREER CENTER
entity_filed: Dean Foods Company (the bankrupt party; unrelated to the grant payee)
same_company_evidence: Not applicable. The headline names Dean Foods, a national dairy processor, and 'Washington County dairy farmers' as the people affected. The payee is a public career-technical school district in Marietta, Washington County, Ohio (EIN 31-0735812, class: government). The only link is the county name.
ohio_outcome: The career center is open and expanding: it cut the ribbon on a new medical-programs expansion in April 2026 and local coverage through October 2026 reports ongoing student programs (SkillsUSA, BPA, FFA officer elections).
source: News and Sentinel headline in the flag; Google News RSS for 'Washington County Career Center' Marietta (WTAP 2026-04-21 ribbon cutting; Marietta Times 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-29)
notes: Classic someone-else's-bankruptcy false positive. Dean Foods filed Chapter 11 on 2019-11-12, four days before the flagged story, and the story is about how local dairy farmers were affected. No insolvency event of any kind for the school district, which could not file an ordinary business bankruptcy in any case.

name: NOSTRUM LABORATORIES INC
entity_filed: Nostrum Laboratories, Inc. (the grant payee itself)
same_company_evidence: Same corporate name and industry. FDA enforcement records (openFDA drug enforcement API) list 'Nostrum Laboratories, Inc.' recalls from both Bryan, OH and Kansas City, MO, confirming the bankrupt pharmaceutical maker is the firm that ran the Bryan, Ohio plant. The grant file gives the payee as NOSTRUM LABORATORIES INC, 705 East Mulberry, Bryan, OH 43506, EIN 20-5877688, Williams County, healthcare. CourtListener docket entries name 'Debtor-in-Possession Nostrum Laboratories, Inc.' and an Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors, so the case is a Chapter 11, not a Chapter 7.
ohio_outcome: Company-wide shutdown. Operations ceased by mid-July 2025; 35 workers were laid off at the Kansas City plant and the firm recalled sucralfate tablets after shutting down. Four approved ANDAs were sold to Strides Pharma in April 2025 and the remaining ANDA portfolio and assets were liquidated against roughly $68 million in debt (reported March 2026). No source found that states the specific fate of the Bryan, Ohio site or its jobs; JobsOhio's 2020 metrics report credited the project with 40 jobs committed and 57 retained on a $3.25 million investment.
source: CourtListener RECAP search result for 'Nostrum Laboratories' (Bankr. D.N.J. 24-19611, filed 2024-09-30, Judge John K. Sherwood, docket text naming the debtor-in-possession and the creditors' committee); openFDA drug enforcement API; Google News RSS (Fierce Pharma 2025-07-16; Kansas City Business Journal 2025-07-17; Medical Dialogues 2025-04-30; ElevenFlo 2026-03-06)
notes: Filed 3.5 years after the first grant year and about three years after the last grant payment, so the failure falls well inside the window. Grants: $157,695 in 2020 and $92,305 in 2021, $250,000 total, both JobsOhio Economic Development Grants (reimbursement-based). Related matter: United States v. Mulye, D. Mass. 1:25-cv-12112, filed 2025-07-28, against founder Nirmal Mulye. Not verified on PACER: CourtListener began returning empty HTTP 202 responses after the first query, so the docket number, court, judge and filing date come from its search index rather than a fetched docket sheet, and the chapter is inferred from docket text ('Debtor-in-Possession', creditors' committee). | The docket header now reads Chapter 7, so the Chapter 11 filed 2024-09-30 converted to liquidation.

name: ACE HARDWARE CORPORATION
entity_filed: An independently owned Ace Hardware retail store in Warsaw, Indiana
same_company_evidence: Not the same company. The flagged story is from timesuniononline.com, the Warsaw Times-Union in Kosciusko County, Indiana, and concerns a single retail store in Warsaw, Indiana holding a liquidation sale. The payee is ACE HARDWARE CORPORATION, EIN 36-0700810, the retailer-owned wholesale cooperative, whose Ohio grant site is its West Jefferson distribution center (a 2018 Business Journals story covers that Central Ohio hiring). Ace's member stores are independently owned, so one closing is not the cooperative failing.
ohio_outcome: The cooperative is growing, not failing: it reported second-quarter 2026 revenue above $3 billion and announced its 100th new store opening of 2026 in September 2026.
source: Google News RSS for 'Ace Hardware Corporation' 2026 (Ace Hardware press release 2026-08-12; Hardware Retailing 2026-08-12; Morningstar 2026-09-02) and for Ace Hardware 'West Jefferson' Ohio (The Business Journals 2018-06-25)
notes: Franchise-store false positive, and the store closing in July 2018 also sits between the two grant years (2015 and 2021). No bankruptcy, receivership or closure by Ace Hardware Corporation itself.

name: Columbus 2020
same_company_evidence: No company match at all. The NBC4 headline reads 'Hard year for business in Columbus 2020: 25 closures, bankruptcies, and struggling businesses', where 'Columbus 2020' is the city name followed by the year. The payee is Columbus 2020, the Columbus region's economic development nonprofit (EIN 27-1509190, class: nonprofit), which is not mentioned in the story.
ohio_outcome: The organization operates today as One Columbus, the economic development organization for the 11-county Columbus Region, which reports having helped more than 670 companies since 2010.
source: NBC4 WCMH-TV headline in the flag; columbusregion.com/one-columbus/about-us/
notes: Pure string coincidence between the nonprofit's name and 'Columbus' plus the year 2020. The entity also changed its public name to One Columbus, which is a rebrand, not a dissolution, and the story itself is about other Columbus businesses closing during the pandemic year.

name: Express Inc
entity_filed: Express, Inc. (the grant payee itself, now renamed EXP OldCo Winddown, Inc.) and certain direct and indirect subsidiaries
same_company_evidence: Exact EIN match. The 2023 Form 10-K of EXP OldCo Winddown, Inc. (f/k/a Express, Inc.) gives IRS Employer Identification No. 26-2828128, matching the payee EIN 262828128, and principal executive offices at 1 Express Drive, Columbus, Ohio 43230, matching the payee city of Columbus, OH.
ohio_outcome: The Columbus headquarters campus, which also houses the company's distribution center, was leased through 2031. The company employed about 10,000 associates as of 2024-02-03; it closed 107 stores and local coverage put roughly 600 Ohio office jobs at risk. The operating business was sold as a going concern in June 2024 to a group led by WHP Global and continues to run the Columbus headquarters; the filing entity itself was wound down.
source: Express, Inc. Form 8-K filed 2024-04-22, Item 1.03 Bankruptcy or Receivership (SEC Archives 0001193125-24-103828); EXP OldCo Winddown, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal 2023 (SEC Archives 0001483510-24-000014), which states the case number and the 2024-12-17 plan confirmation; Google News RSS (AP/10TV 2024-06-17; CBS News 2024-04-22; WLWT 2024-04-24)
notes: Filed eight years after the single 2016 grant year, so comfortably inside the window. The 8-K describes voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the District of Delaware and about $162.6 million of debtor-in-possession ABL financing from Wells Fargo. The bankruptcy court confirmed a joint plan of reorganization on 2024-12-17 under which sale proceeds and remaining assets are distributed to claim holders and each debtor's estate is wound down. The registrant deregistered its stock on 2024-04-24 (Form 15) and renamed itself EXP OldCo Winddown, Inc. This is a corporate failure with a going-concern sale, not a liquidation of the brand.

name: CHERYL & CO
same_company_evidence: No match. The flagged item is a Daily Mail celebrity story about footballer Wes Brown dating a lookalike of the British singer Cheryl Cole; 'Cheryl' and a surname are the only overlap with the payee's name. The payee is CHERYL & CO (Cheryl's Cookies), EIN 31-1006364, Obetz, Ohio, a bakery owned by 1-800-FLOWERS.COM, Inc.
ohio_outcome: Nothing in the flagged story or in searches of Obetz and Cheryl's Cookies coverage reports a closure, bankruptcy or layoff at the Obetz bakery.
source: Daily Mail headline in the flag; Google News RSS for 'Cheryl & Co' Obetz and for 'Cheryl's Cookies' Obetz, which return only obituaries, a 2018 trademark suit against founder Cheryl Krueger's new venture, and 1-800-Flowers seasonal hiring stories
notes: Celebrity-gossip false positive; the scanner matched on the name fragment and a word in the headline, not on any insolvency event. Nothing about the payee or its parent, 1-800-FLOWERS.COM, Inc., is in the story, and no bankruptcy filing by either was found.

name: ROCKY BRANDS INC
entity_filed: West Marine (the bankrupt party; Rocky Brands appears only as a creditor)
same_company_evidence: Identity confirmed and the roles are the opposite of a failure. SEC EDGAR lists ROCKY BRANDS, INC. (CIK 0000895456) with EIN 31-1364046, matching the payee EIN, and a business address in Nelsonville, Ohio, matching the payee city. Both flagged headlines describe Rocky Brands as a creditor owed about $1.1 million in West Marine's bankruptcy, alongside Luxottica.
ohio_outcome: Rocky Brands is an active SEC registrant and operating normally; it filed an 8-K on 2026-10-27 with third-quarter 2026 results and continues to run its Nelsonville, Ohio operations.
source: SEC EDGAR submissions API, CIK 0000895456 (EIN 311364046, Nelsonville; most recent 8-K 2026-10-27); Google News RSS (WWD 2026-05-20; Fashion United 2026-05-21; Yahoo Finance Q3 earnings 2026-10-28)
notes: Textbook creditor false positive, the same pattern as a bank appearing in someone else's case. Being owed money in a customer's bankruptcy is a loss, not an insolvency, and the company has filed continuously with the SEC since.

name: EARTHQUAKER DEVICES LLC
same_company_evidence: Same company, right city: the Akron Beacon Journal story is explicitly about 'Akron-based EarthQuaker Devices' and quotes its CEO, matching the payee EARTHQUAKER DEVICES LLC of Akron, Ohio. The identification is not in doubt; the event is.
ohio_outcome: Still operating in Akron. Trade coverage shows new product releases through 2026, including the Bellows Fuzz Driver in July 2026 and a MOSFET version of the Plumes Jr. in October 2026.
source: Google News RSS for 'EarthQuaker Devices' bankruptcy (Akron Beacon Journal 2025-05-18; Guitar World 2025-05-21; Gearnews.com 2026-07-06 and 2026-10-29)
notes: Conditional, forward-looking language in the headline, not an event. The CEO said tariffs 'could lead to bankruptcy' and that the business was 'at risk of going bankrupt amid tariff uncertainty'; no petition, receivership, assignment or closure followed. Searches found no bankruptcy case and the company was shipping new pedals 17 months later. Worth a second look if coverage changes, but as of now there is nothing to report.

name: GOODLEVEL ENTERPRISES LLC
entity_filed: Goodlevel Enterprises Canada ULC, an apparent affiliate, not the grant payee
court: Canadian insolvency proceeding under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (proposal; KPMG acting as trustee). Not a U.S. bankruptcy court.
same_company_evidence: Not established. The payee is GOODLEVEL ENTERPRISES LLC, EIN 81-4719550, 55 Newton St, Norwalk, OH 44857, an advanced-manufacturing small business credited with 74 jobs retained and 63 Form 5500 participants in 2023. The insolvent entity is a separately incorporated Canadian company, Goodlevel Enterprises Canada ULC. The shared name suggests common ownership, but no document was found that states the corporate relationship, and nothing ties the Ohio LLC to the Canadian filing.
ohio_outcome: Unknown. No news, WARN notice or other record of a closure, layoff or insolvency at the Norwalk, Ohio operation was found.
source: Google News RSS for 'Goodlevel Enterprises' and 'Goodlevel', which return only two items, both about the Canadian entity (Insolvency Insider Canada 2025-08-25 'Goodlevel Enterprises Canada ULC, Proposal'; kpmg.com 2026-02-24); JobsOhio grant records in data/grants_raw.csv and data/parents.csv
notes: Could not be settled. Both source pages are unreachable: the Insolvency Insider article URL now 404s and its site search returns nothing for Goodlevel, the KPMG creditor-information page for the case 404s at every path tried, the Wayback CDX index has no archived kpmg.com URL containing 'goodlevel', and the Google News article links resolve only to Google's own JavaScript wrapper. A privately held Ohio LLC files no SEC reports, and CourtListener had started returning empty HTTP 202 responses, so no U.S. docket check was possible. The honest reading is that a Canadian sister company filed a Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act proposal in August 2025, two years after the 2023 Inclusion Grant, with no evidence either way about the Norwalk plant. An earlier pass in data/research/sub_07.json reached the same conclusion, calling the Canadian entity 'an affiliate rather than an owner'. Settling this needs a PACER or Canadian OSB name search, or a call to the Norwalk plant.
